featured.title: Fifteen Indian Tourists Died When Their Speedboat Capsized off Vietnam. The Victims Were on a Company Trip.
featured.excerpt: A criminal investigation is underway, bodies are being repatriated, and the tragedy is raising hard questions about tourist safety in Southeast Asia.
featured.image_caption: Long Beach on Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam, where a speedboat carrying 32 Indian tourists capsized on July 11
featured.nri_angle: Fifteen Indian nationals — employees of a mobile phone company from Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and other southern states — were killed on a group excursion, prompting a massive consular operation and raising safety concerns for the millions of Indians who travel to Southeast Asia each year.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Fifteen Indian Tourists Died When Their Speedboat Capsized off Vietnam. The Victims Were on a Company Trip.
news.excerpt: A criminal investigation is underway, bodies are being repatriated, and the tragedy is raising hard questions about tourist safety in Southeast Asia.
news.image_caption: Long Beach on Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam, where a speedboat carrying 32 Indian tourists capsized on July 11
news.nri_angle: Fifteen Indian nationals — employees of a mobile phone company from Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and other southern states — were killed on a group excursion, prompting a massive consular operation and raising safety concerns for the millions of Indians who travel to Southeast Asia each year.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Summoned Iran's Envoy Over the Killing of an Indian Sailor in the Hormuz Strait. The Death Toll Is Still Rising.
news.excerpt: New Delhi lodged a formal protest after Iranian missiles killed one Indian and wounded ten more on two UAE tankers. Another Indian is still missing from a separate attack.
news.image_caption: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar; the foreign ministry summoned Iran's deputy ambassador on Tuesday
news.nri_angle: India has roughly nine million nationals in the Gulf and hundreds of thousands of seafarers who transit the Strait of Hormuz. With Indian crew members now being killed and wounded in missile strikes, New Delhi's formal protest to Iran signals a harder diplomatic line on a crisis that directly threatens diaspora lives.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Lindsey Graham, the Senate's Loudest Voice on Iran and India, Dies at 71. His Empty Chair Changes the Calculus for Both.
news.excerpt: The South Carolina senator — Budget Committee chairman, immigration deal-maker, and the man who pressed Trump hardest on the Iran war now shaping life for nine million Indians in the Gulf — died of cardiac arrest Saturday night, a day after meeting Zelensky in Kyiv.
news.image_caption: Senator Lindsey Graham in his official 113th Congress portrait
news.nri_angle: Graham shaped key immigration policy including H-1B visa reform debates, championed the US-India defense partnership, and drove the Iran war policy now directly affecting nine million Indians in the Gulf — his absence shifts Senate dynamics on all three fronts.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian Sailor Was Killed When Iranian Missiles Hit Two UAE Tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Six More Indians Were Wounded.
news.excerpt: The strikes on the Mombasa and Al Bahiyah mark the first confirmed death of an Indian national in direct combat action during the Gulf war. For 90,000 Indian seafarers in the region, the waterway they transit daily has become a battlefield.
news.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian missiles struck two UAE oil tankers on Monday
news.nri_angle: An Indian seafarer was killed and six were wounded in the Gulf — for 90,000 Indian mariners in the region and their families back home, the war is no longer abstract.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Trump Just Slapped a 20% Toll on the World's Most Important Waterway. India's Oil Bill Could Jump by Billions.
news.excerpt: India imports nearly 85% of its crude oil, much of it through the Strait of Hormuz. The president's 'Guardian' declaration and cargo fee threaten to blow open the trade deficit, weaken the rupee, and push inflation past the central bank's red line — all at once.
news.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, through which nearly a third of the world's seaborne oil flows — and now subject to a 20% US transit toll
news.nri_angle: India imports 85% of its crude oil, much through Hormuz — a 20% toll could add $15B to the annual import bill, weaken the rupee, raise inflation, and erode the purchasing power of remittances for millions of NRI families.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Hosting Iran, Russia, and China Under One Roof While American Missiles Hit the Gulf. Welcome to the BRICS Presidency.
news.excerpt: As ministerial meetings stack up across Delhi and Nagpur ahead of September's summit, India's BRICS chairmanship is becoming a real-time test of Modi's diplomatic balancing act — with the diaspora's safety and prosperity on the line.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi at a BRICS Leaders' meeting in expanded format
news.nri_angle: India's ability to maintain working relationships with both Washington and Tehran through the BRICS presidency directly determines the safety of nine million Indians in the Gulf, the stability of energy prices affecting diaspora families, and the remittance corridors that fund communities back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Biggest Crackdown on Indian Crime in U.S. History Just Swept Three Continents. Here Is What It Means for the Diaspora.
news.excerpt: Operation Hard Ball charged 37 people tied to the Bishnoi and Bhagwanpuria gangs with racketeering, political assassination, and drug trafficking — and prosecutors say the investigation is far from over.
news.image_caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the federal prosecutors who led Operation Hard Ball
news.nri_angle: Indian American communities in California and across the U.S. were directly targeted by the syndicates through extortion, drug trafficking, and intimidation, making this the most significant law-enforcement action to confront transnational Indian organised crime on American soil.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Six Thousand Seafarers Are Trapped in the Gulf. For Indian Sailors, the War Has Become Personal.
news.excerpt: Three Indian crew members are dead. One sailor watched 140 missiles fly in 30 minutes. Thousands more are stranded on ships running low on food and fuel. India is sending diplomats. The sailors want a way home.
news.image_caption: Satellite image of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman where thousands of ships and seafarers remain stranded
news.nri_angle: Roughly 23,000 Indians work on merchant and offshore vessels in the Gulf region — India is one of the world's top three suppliers of seafarers, and the Iran war has killed three Indian crew members while trapping thousands more on ships under fire.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Oil Jumps 3%, Rupee Slides, Sensex Sinks. For Indian Families Sending Money Home, the War Just Got Personal.
news.excerpt: Monday's market open delivered the economic reality of the weekend's Gulf escalation — Brent crude above $78, the rupee headed for 95.60, and all 16 sectors in the red. NRI remittances are about to buy less.
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, the barometer of India's market anxiety
news.nri_angle: NRI remittances, Gulf worker safety, and the purchasing power of savings sent home to Indian families are all directly threatened by the oil-driven market selloff.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Sold Its Most Powerful Missile to a Third Country. The $630 Million Deal Rewrites the Indo-Pacific Arms Map.
news.excerpt: Indonesia becomes the third nation to buy the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile, after the Philippines and Vietnam. India's defence exports have grown thirty-five-fold in a decade.
news.image_caption: BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system on display during India's Republic Day parade in New Delhi
news.nri_angle: India's transformation from the world's largest arms importer to a meaningful defence exporter — with combat-proven systems now deployed across Southeast Asia — marks a generational shift in the country's global standing that NRIs have long advocated for.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian Immigrant's Son Launches to the Space Station on Monday. He Spent a Year in India Vaccinating Children Against Polio.
news.excerpt: NASA astronaut Anil Menon — born to a Kerala-origin father and a Ukrainian mother in Minneapolis — lifts off aboard Soyuz MS-29 on July 14 for an eight-month mission. He is a Harvard neuroscientist, Stanford physician, former SpaceX flight surgeon, and the latest in a growing line of Indian-origin Americans reaching orbit.
news.image_caption: NASA astronaut Anil Menon in his official portrait at Johnson Space Center
news.nri_angle: Menon is the son of an Indian immigrant from Kerala and spent a formative year in India on a Rotary scholarship fighting polio — his launch is one of the most visible achievements by an Indian-American in the US space programme, following Kalpana Chawla, Sunita Williams, and Raja Chari.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: While India's Navy Guards the Gulf, Its Tall Ship Is Celebrating America's Birthday in Boston
news.excerpt: INS Sudarshini has sailed 13,000 nautical miles from Kochi to join sixty warships and tall ships in Boston Harbour for America's 250th anniversary — the biggest peacetime maritime gathering in decades.
news.image_caption: INS Sudarshini, the Indian Navy's sail training ship, now at Sail Boston 250 for America's 250th anniversary
news.nri_angle: INS Sudarshini is open to the public in Boston through July 16 — a rare chance for Indian Americans in New England to board an Indian naval vessel on American soil.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The European Parliament Just Condemned Pakistan for the Forced Conversion of Hindu and Christian Girls. The Numbers Are Staggering.
news.excerpt: Seventy-five per cent of forced conversion victims in Pakistan are Hindu. The EU resolution calls out a court ruling that validated the marriage of a 13-year-old Christian girl to her 30-year-old abductor.
news.image_caption: The European Parliament hemicycle in Strasbourg, France, where members voted on the resolution condemning forced conversions in Pakistan
news.nri_angle: Seventy-five per cent of Pakistan's forced conversion victims are Hindu — the EU resolution reinforces concerns held by the Indian diaspora and backs India's long-standing push for minority rights protection in Pakistan.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An ICE Agent Fatally Shot an Authorized Worker in Maine. It Was the Second Killing in a Week.
news.excerpt: The 26-year-old Colombian man had a Social Security number and legal work authorization. His death in Biddeford came days after agents killed a Mexican national in Houston. For immigrant communities — including hundreds of thousands of Indians — the enforcement escalation has turned routine encounters into life-or-death moments.
news.image_caption: ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations agents during a field operation in Florida, February 2025
news.image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
news.nri_angle: Two ICE killings in a week — both involving men with legal status or work authorization — signal an enforcement climate that Indian H-1B holders and green card applicants cannot ignore.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Iran War Just Went Gulf-Wide. For Nine Million Indians in the Region, the Fight Is Now Overhead.
news.excerpt: Iranian missiles struck targets in five Gulf states in a single day. The U.S. hit 300 targets in three nights. The Strait of Hormuz is closed again. And India's largest overseas community is caught in the middle.
news.image_caption: A U.S. Navy supply vessel transits the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil supply passes
news.nri_angle: Nine million Indians in the Gulf — the largest expatriate community in the region — are directly affected as Iranian strikes expand to five countries where they live and work, while 6,000 Indian seafarers remain stranded and Gulf remittances worth $28 billion face disruption.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Supreme Court Just Saved Birthright Citizenship. For Half a Million Indian Families on Temporary Visas, It Was Never Abstract.
news.excerpt: A 6-3 ruling strikes down Trump's executive order denying automatic citizenship to children born to H-1B, H-4, and other temporary visa holders — preserving a right that quietly underpins Indian America.
news.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C.
news.nri_angle: Over 5.4 million Indian Americans, most on temporary visas with decades-long green card waits, would have seen their U.S.-born children denied citizenship had the order stood.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Iran Just Closed the Strait of Hormuz 'Until Further Notice.' India Has Spent Four Months Preparing for Exactly This.
news.excerpt: A struck vessel, a formal closure, and a collapsing ceasefire — but India's petroleum minister says the country's crisis playbook has kept pumps open and prices lower than anywhere in the world.
news.image_caption: Satellite or aerial view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which a fifth of the world's oil once flowed
news.nri_angle: Six thousand Indian seafarers remain trapped in the Gulf, and the closure threatens India's fragile energy recovery — raising inflation, weakening the rupee, and straining supply lines that NRI remittances help sustain.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Approved Its Biggest Emergency Oil Stockpile in a Decade. The Hormuz Blockade Made the Case.
news.excerpt: ONGC will build a 1.75 million tonne underground crude reserve at Mangalore — expanding India's emergency buffer by a third — after the Strait of Hormuz crisis exposed how little fuel the country can store.
news.image_caption: An underground strategic petroleum reserve cavern — India is building similar facilities to buffer its emergency oil supply
news.nri_angle: India's oil storage capacity directly affects fuel prices, cooking gas costs, and inflation that erode the value of NRI remittances and savings sent home to families.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Thirty-Seven Defendants, Three Gangs, One Assassination: Inside the US Indictment That Finally Named Nijjar's Killers
nri-world.excerpt: Operation Hardball charges Lawrence Bishnoi with directing the 2023 murder of a Sikh leader from an Indian prison cell. India says it will cooperate. The diaspora is still counting the cost.
nri-world.image_caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the federal prosecutors who unsealed the Bishnoi indictment
nri-world.nri_angle: The Bishnoi gang systematically used high-profile killings to terrorize the Indian diaspora in North America, targeting religious, social, and political leaders. The indictment is the most significant legal action yet addressing transnational criminal threats to Sikh and Indian communities abroad.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Indian Grocery Store Burned Before It Opened. A Mosque Replica Set Ablaze on a Bonfire. Inside Northern Ireland's Summer of Hate.
nri-world.excerpt: Belfast's June riots left 27 people homeless and an Indian community shaken. A month later, the arsonists have moved on to bonfires — and the 10,000 Indians in Northern Ireland are still waiting for the institutions to catch up.
nri-world.image_caption: Belfast, Northern Ireland — where anti-immigrant riots in June 2026 shattered the Indian community's sense of safety (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: Northern Ireland's Indian community — roughly 10,000 people, many of them doctors, shopkeepers, and IT professionals who chose Belfast for its affordability — found itself at the centre of anti-immigrant riots in June 2026. The violence, including the arson of an Indian grocery store, exposed the growing vulnerability of diaspora communities in the UK.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: One Indian Sailor Missing, Ten Rescued After Iran Strikes Container Ship in the Strait of Hormuz
nri-world.excerpt: The attack on the GFS Galaxy is the fourth time in three months that a vessel with Indian crew has been hit in the Hormuz standoff. India's 300,000-strong seafaring community is running out of safe passage.
nri-world.image_caption: Naval vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, where Indian-crewed commercial ships have repeatedly been struck since April 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian seafarers — over 300,000 strong — are disproportionately exposed to the Hormuz standoff. Four ships with Indian crews have been struck since April. Maritime families in coastal India and across the diaspora live with a unique anxiety each time a vessel is hit.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India-UK Trade Deal Goes Live on July 15 — What Changes for NRIs in Britain
nri-world.excerpt: The new trade pact eliminates dual social security contributions for Indian workers in the UK, saves them roughly 25 per cent of salary, and opens 1,800 annual mobility slots for chefs, yoga instructors, and classical musicians.
nri-world.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds at the signing of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
nri-world.nri_angle: 75,000+ Indian professionals in Britain stand to save roughly 25 per cent of salary through the social security pact, while new mobility pathways and tariff reductions reshape the economic relationship between the diaspora's two largest host countries.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Tax Department Can Now See Your Foreign Bank Accounts. Here Is What Every NRI Needs to Know.
nri-world.excerpt: A CBDT order integrates overseas financial data from over a hundred countries into taxpayers' Annual Information Statements, closing one of the last gaps in cross-border tax visibility.
nri-world.image_caption: Aaykar Bhavan, the Income Tax Department's office in Pune, India
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs with bank accounts, investments, or property in India now face unprecedented transparency — their overseas financial information from the US, UK, Canada, and other AEOI countries will appear in their Indian tax records, raising the compliance stakes for the 30-million-strong diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: From Fremont to Parsippany: Indian-Origin Mayors Are Making History Across America
nri-world.excerpt: Raj Salwan and Pulkit Desai lead a growing wave of Indian Americans winning local elections, reflecting the community's deepening civic roots.
nri-world.image_caption: Raj Salwan, the first Indian American mayor of Fremont, California
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian Americans are translating decades of private-sector success into local political leadership, with first-generation immigrants winning mayoral races in diverse cities from California to New Jersey.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian American Neurologist Wins Lifetime Achievement Award for Transforming Global Stroke Care
nri-world.excerpt: Dr. Dileep Yavagal, founder of Mission Thrombectomy active in over ninety countries, honoured for reshaping how the world treats the leading cause of disability.
nri-world.image_caption: Dr. Dileep Yavagal, based at the University of Miami, received a Lifetime Achievement Award for transforming global stroke care
nri-world.nri_angle: Yavagal's career traces the circuit of the Indian medical diaspora — training in India, research breakthroughs at American institutions, and a global initiative that channels those advances back to underserved communities worldwide, including in South Asia.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Indian-Origin Leaders Tapped to Co-Lead Federal Reserve Policy Task Forces
nri-world.excerpt: Raghuram Rajan, Raj Chetty, and Xbox CEO Sarah Bond (born Asha Sharma) will co-chair three of the Fed's five review panels — an unprecedented concentration of diaspora talent at the heart of U.S. monetary policy.
nri-world.image_caption: Raghuram Rajan, former RBI Governor and IMF Chief Economist, will co-chair the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet Policy review
nri-world.nri_angle: Three Indian-origin figures simultaneously co-leading Federal Reserve policy review panels — spanning economics, data science, and corporate leadership — signals the breadth of diaspora influence in U.S. economic policymaking.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian American Congressman Ro Khanna Detained at Gunpoint by Israeli Settlers in West Bank
nri-world.excerpt: The Silicon Valley lawmaker — a potential 2028 presidential candidate and grandson of an Indian freedom fighter — says IDF soldiers sided with the armed settlers who held his group for 75 minutes.
nri-world.image_caption: Congressman Ro Khanna, who represents California's 17th congressional district in Silicon Valley
nri-world.nri_angle: Khanna is among the most prominent Indian Americans in U.S. politics, a potential 2028 presidential candidate whose family story — from a freedom fighter's household in Punjab to Silicon Valley — embodies the trajectory of the Indian diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Eleven Thousand Years of India, One Museum in Washington: The Diaspora's Audacious Bid to Tell Its Own Story
nri-world.excerpt: An Atlanta-based educationist has spent eight years building a case for a $14 million heritage centre in the American capital. He has now asked the Indian Embassy for a building it bought thirteen years ago.
nri-world.image_caption: The Embassy of India in Washington, D.C., where organisers have proposed housing the heritage museum
nri-world.nri_angle: A first-of-its-kind museum aimed at helping younger Indian Americans connect with their civilisational heritage, built by and for the diaspora
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: One Hundred and Fifty Dancers, Seventeen Countries, Three Nights Under the Acropolis: Inside the World Festival of Indian Dance
nri-world.excerpt: The fourth edition of the UNESCO-endorsed classical Indian dance festival opens in Athens this week, with performers from the United States, Canada, Britain, Oman, South Africa, and a dozen other nations gathering at the foot of Western civilisation's most famous monument.
nri-world.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer performing at the Khajuraho Dance Festival earlier in 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian classical dance traditions carried and performed by diaspora communities across 17 countries, showcasing how NRIs preserve and project cultural heritage on a global stage
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Sunil Bharti Mittal Calls Indian Diaspora a 'Beautiful Bridge' as USISPF Honours Him with Leadership Award
nri-world.excerpt: The Bharti Enterprises founder was honoured alongside RTX's Christopher Calio and Fairfax Financial's V. Prem Watsa at the IX USISPF Leadership Summit in Washington.
nri-world.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal at the USISPF Leadership Summit
nri-world.nri_angle: Mittal's speech directly celebrated the five-million-strong Indian diaspora in the US as the connective tissue between the two nations, with trade deal implications for NRI business leaders.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: RBI's NRI Deposit Drive Crosses $10 Billion — But the Real Flood Is Coming Before the September Deadline
markets-finance.excerpt: India's special FCNR scheme for overseas Indians has raised $10 billion so far, with economists expecting $30–60 billion by the September 30 cutoff as the rupee weakens past 96.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, where policymakers designed the NRI deposit programme to bolster forex reserves
markets-finance.nri_angle: FCNR deposits carry zero currency risk for NRIs, and with the rupee at 96.20/USD and banks offering competitive yields under the RBI swap facility, the programme represents one of the best NRI deposit windows in years — but the September 30 deadline is firm.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Fairfax Submits Revised Bid for IDBI Bank — India's Biggest Bank Privatization Could Close Within a Month
markets-finance.excerpt: Canada's Fairfax Financial is the frontrunner to acquire a 60.7% stake in the $9.67 billion lender, reviving a deal that stalled over valuation in March.
markets-finance.image_caption: Prem Watsa, Hyderabad-born billionaire and Fairfax Financial chairman, who is the frontrunner to acquire IDBI Bank
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs holding IDBI accounts could see upgraded services under private ownership, while the deal signals India is finally serious about bank privatization — reshaping a sector where 55% of assets remain state-controlled.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: SEBI Wants to Double the Stocks You Can Short — And India's $5 Trillion Market Is About to Get a Lot More Interesting for NRIs
markets-finance.excerpt: India's market regulator is planning to nearly double stocks eligible for lending and borrowing from 176 to over 300, while cutting collateral from 130% to near-global levels — a move aimed at pulling retail investors away from the world's largest and riskiest derivatives market.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India's oldest stock exchange
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors trading Indian equities through PIS accounts and GIFT City brokerages will benefit from deeper cash market liquidity and lower margin requirements, making hedging positions cheaper and more flexible
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Bond Market Awaits a $25 Billion Catalyst — Bloomberg Global Index Decision Expected This Month
markets-finance.excerpt: Foreign investors have poured $4.1 billion into Indian bonds in six weeks. If Bloomberg adds India to its flagship Global Aggregate Index, the floodgates could open — reshaping yields, the rupee, and NRI fixed-income portfolios.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, central to India's bond market policy
markets-finance.nri_angle: Bloomberg inclusion would compress Indian bond yields, strengthen the rupee, and benefit NRIs holding government bonds, gilt funds, and NRE/NRO fixed deposits. The resulting passive foreign demand could add $20-25 billion to India's debt market.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: TCS Reshuffles Its Top Brass and Creates Five New Business Units — Here's What the AI-Era Overhaul Means for NRI Investors
markets-finance.excerpt: India's largest IT services company splits its American banking unit in two, carves out a dedicated US West Coast business, and bets big on ServiceNow and autonomous operations as AI threatens to reshape the $315 billion sector.
markets-finance.image_caption: TCS campus in Madhapur, Hyderabad — headquarters of the company's sprawling operations
markets-finance.nri_angle: TCS is the single largest Indian IT stock by market cap (~$145B) and a staple in NRI equity portfolios. The reorganization — splitting the BFSI Americas unit, creating a US West Coast business group, and building a standalone ServiceNow practice — directly targets the American market where most NRIs live and work. Understanding the strategic pivot is essential for anyone holding or considering TCS shares.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Banks Race for Global Ratings as RBI's FCNR Dollar Drive Opens a Rare Window for NRI Depositors
markets-finance.excerpt: Federal Bank, YES Bank, and Bank of Baroda have secured international credit ratings to attract NRI deposits, while the RBI's special swap window offers up to 7.1% on dollar deposits — tax-free — until September 30.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs holding surplus dollars in low-yielding US savings accounts have a time-limited opportunity to earn 6-7% in dollar terms through FCNR(B) deposits at internationally rated Indian banks — tax-free under Indian law, fully repatriable. Window closes September 30, 2026.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Sensex Drops 560 Points as Brent Crude Hits $87 and Rupee Slides Past 96 — What NRIs Need to Know About the Oil Shock
markets-finance.excerpt: India's markets buckle under renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities, with 12 of 16 sectors in the red and the rupee at its weakest in over a month.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, where the Sensex dropped 0.72% on Tuesday amid oil shock fears
markets-finance.nri_angle: The rupee near 96.20/USD creates a favourable remittance window, but erodes dollar-denominated returns on Indian equity and NRE deposits. NRIs with dual-economy portfolios face a stress test across currencies, oil, and equities.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: One in Five Ultra-Rich Indians Are Planning to Move Abroad — And It's Quietly Reshaping the NRI Financial Landscape
markets-finance.excerpt: A new Kotak Bank report reveals that 20% of India's ultra-high-net-worth individuals are migrating permanently while retaining citizenship, as India ranks third globally in millionaire outflows — behind China and the UK.
markets-finance.image_caption: Dubai Marina at night — the UAE has become the world's top destination for migrating millionaires
markets-finance.nri_angle: The Ultra-HNIs leaving India today are becoming tomorrow's NRIs — reshaping wealth management demand, FEMA compliance complexity, and cross-border financial infrastructure that all 32 million diaspora members navigate.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Gold ETF Boom Hits a Wall — Fund Houses Cap Purchases as Physical Demand Cools and Discounts Widen
markets-finance.excerpt: Gold ETF assets nearly tripled to ₹1.85 lakh crore, but six major AMCs have capped subscriptions. Meanwhile, Mumbai dealers are offering $19-per-ounce discounts. Here's what NRI gold investors should know.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold bullion bar at the Swiss Money Museum
markets-finance.image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / Ank Kumar, CC BY-SA 4.0
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI gold investors face a shifting landscape: ETF subscription caps force larger allocators to split across AMCs, Sovereign Gold Bonds remain the best vehicle for tax-efficient exposure, and a weak rupee inflates India gold prices for dollar earners.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's IT Stocks Stage a 10% July Rally as AI Deals Reshape the Sector — Why the Street Is Still Skeptical
markets-finance.excerpt: TCS, HCLTech, and LTIMindtree surged on Monday as Anthropic partnerships and a mega ABB deal gave the beaten-down sector its best month of 2026 — but analysts warn this is trading, not conviction.
markets-finance.image_caption: The glass pyramid at Infosys campus in Bangalore, a symbol of India's IT industry
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors hold significant IT stock exposure through direct equity and ETFs; AI partnerships could signal a structural shift or just a bear market bounce — the distinction matters for long-term portfolios.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Isn't Rushing Into a US Trade Deal — And Goldman Sachs Just Gave Modi Another Reason to Wait
markets-finance.excerpt: With exports up 15%, a UK free trade pact about to kick in, and an upgraded 6.8% growth forecast, New Delhi is playing the long game on tariffs — even as Washington threatens to raise the stakes this month.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has described the trade talks as balanced and productive
markets-finance.image_credit: Government of India / Wikimedia Commons, GODL-India
markets-finance.nri_angle: Trade deal impacts IT services revenue (50-60% from US), bilateral trade aspiration to $500B affects NRI entrepreneurs, and trade uncertainty contributes to rupee volatility affecting remittances and NRE deposits.

markets-finance.title: India Scraps Import Duties on Smartphone Parts and Lithium-Ion Cells — A $500 Billion Bet on Becoming the World's Electronics Factory

technology.title: Washington Is About to Rewrite the H-1B Playbook. Indian IT Giants Should Be Worried.
technology.excerpt: A sweeping regulatory package expected in August would tighten third-party placements, raise Green Card wage floors, and end open-ended student stays. For TCS, Infosys, and Wipro, the operating model itself is on trial.
technology.image_caption: The United States Capitol building at dusk in Washington, D.C.
technology.nri_angle: Indians account for 73 per cent of all approved H-1B petitions. The proposed rules directly target the third-party placement model used by Indian IT firms and would raise costs for Green Card sponsorship, restrict student work permits, and create gaps in spousal employment authorisation.

technology.title: Satya Nadella Is Quietly Building Microsoft's Own AI Models. The Goal: Stop Paying OpenAI and Anthropic.

technology.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, who has reportedly said he feared Microsoft becoming 'the next IBM'
technology.nri_angle: Satya Nadella, the Indian-born CEO who transformed Microsoft, is making the boldest strategic bet of his tenure. For the thousands of Indian engineers at Microsoft's Hyderabad and Bangalore offices working on AI, MAI could determine the trajectory of their careers.

A restructure that carves out a dedicated U.S. West Coast unit and splits the banking vertical — the company's single largest revenue stream — directly reshapes career paths, reporting lines, and visa sponsorship structures for Indian tech workers from Wall Street to the Bay Area.

lifestyle-health.title: One in Three Asian Americans With Serious Distress Goes Untreated, Largest NYC Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A population-based study of 6,648 Asian American adults in New York City found that stigma, cost, and a lack of culturally matched therapists are leaving a fast-growing community without the mental health care it needs.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The cultural barriers to mental health care identified in this NYC study — stigma, self-reliance, lack of matched therapists — are replicated across South Asian communities in the US, Canada, and UK, compounding the diaspora's already elevated cardiovascular risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Daily Cup of Dahi and a 30-Minute Walk May Slow Aging at the Cellular Level, Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A clinical trial published in Aging showed that yogurt, moderate exercise, and dietary tweaks reduced the pace of biological aging by 2.2% in just 12 weeks — independent of weight loss.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A bowl of yogurt — consuming 100 grams daily was part of the anti-aging intervention studied by researchers (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Dahi (plain yogurt) has been a daily staple in Indian households for generations — this clinical trial validates that the tradition may carry real anti-aging benefits at the cellular level.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Structured Lifestyle Changes Improved Brain Health by 55% in At-Risk Adults, Landmark AAIC Study Shows
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The LatAm-FINGERS trial, presented at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference 2026 in London and published in The Lancet, found that coached exercise, adapted diets, cognitive training, and social engagement dramatically boosted memory and thinking in older adults across 11 countries.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An fMRI brain scan — a landmark AAIC study found structured lifestyle changes improved cognitive function by 55% in at-risk adults (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated dementia risk factors by midlife. This landmark trial shows that the coached lifestyle changes most effective for brain health — group exercise, adapted diets, social engagement — mirror traditions already embedded in diaspora communities.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: South Asians Face Higher Heart Risk by 45 Despite Healthier Habits, Major Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A decade-long Northwestern study of 2,700 adults reveals a troubling paradox: South Asians report better diets and lower alcohol use but develop prediabetes and hypertension at double the rate of white Americans by midlife.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A blood pressure screening — a major new study finds South Asians face significantly higher cardiovascular risk by age 45 (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian Americans face uniquely elevated cardiovascular risk that standard BMI and lifestyle metrics fail to capture, demanding earlier screening and culturally tailored health interventions.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: 14 Indian Cities Rank Among the World's Most Heat-Vulnerable. Here's What That Means for Your Family Back Home.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new Oxford University analysis of cities at greatest risk from extreme heat placed Nagpur, Chennai, Bengaluru, and 11 other Indian cities in the global top 50 — driven not just by soaring temperatures but by limited infrastructure, aging populations, and socioeconomic vulnerability.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Indian cities face compounding heat risks from soaring temperatures and limited cooling infrastructure
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs with aging parents in any of 14 Indian cities ranked among the world's most heat-vulnerable need a concrete plan — from cooling infrastructure to medication reviews — before the next summer peak.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: From Bhag Club to Bombay On Foot: How India's Run Club Boom Is Rewriting the Wellness Playbook
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Across India's cities, running clubs are replacing bar crawls as the new social ritual — and the movement is resonating with the diaspora seeking community beyond the treadmill.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Runners gather for an early morning group run in an Indian city park
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs watching India's community fitness explosion are finding parallels in their own cities — and many are launching or joining similar run clubs abroad, bridging diaspora loneliness with the Indian ethos of collective wellness.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Science Is Settling: What 104 Clinical Trials Say About Turmeric's Real Health Benefits
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A sweeping meta-analysis of over 100 randomized controlled trials finds that curcumin supplementation significantly lowers blood sugar, cholesterol, and inflammation — but the dose and form matter more than your grandmother's golden milk recipe.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh turmeric root and ground curcumin powder, staples of South Asian kitchens
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For South Asians who grew up with turmeric as kitchen medicine, the largest-ever clinical review validates what their grandmothers always said — while revealing that traditional culinary doses and modern supplements are not the same thing.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: An Anti-Inflammatory Diet Cut Dementia Risk by 29% — and Your Dadi's Kitchen Had It Right All Along
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark 15-year study in JAMA Network Open found that diets rich in vegetables, legumes, and whole grains — staples of traditional South Asian cooking — significantly lower the odds of cognitive decline, even in people already showing early signs of Alzheimer's.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh vegetables, legumes, and whole grains — staples of anti-inflammatory eating patterns linked to lower dementia risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Traditional South Asian diets rich in anti-inflammatory ingredients like turmeric, dal, and whole grains align closely with the eating pattern shown to cut dementia risk — a critical finding for a community at elevated cardiometabolic risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Five Weeks of Walking With Poles Cut Depression Symptoms in Half, a Landmark Trial Found
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A randomized controlled trial published in the Journal of Affective Disorders found that supervised Nordic walking led to clinical remission in up to 53% of participants — offering a low-cost, stigma-free path to mental health care that could resonate in South Asian communities.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Nordic walking engages up to 90 percent of the body's muscles, turning a simple walk into a full-body workout
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Community walking groups are already a fixture in South Asian diaspora neighborhoods — this study suggests adding structure to what people already do could yield clinical-grade mental health benefits in a culturally comfortable, stigma-free way.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

food.nri_angle: The IHA designation validates what NRI families have known for generations — Indian spices are not folk remedies but scientifically validated health powerhouses, now driving a multibillion-dollar global wellness industry.

food.excerpt: From a 20,000-square-foot anchor store in Florida to a former Big Lots in Ohio, Indian grocery chains are expanding at a pace that mirrors the diaspora's own growth — and they are reshaping how America shops for food.

food.nri_angle: Indian grocery expansion in suburban America is the infrastructure of belonging — when Patel Brothers opens in your suburb, it means home is a little closer.

travel.title: Fifteen Indian Tourists Killed in Vietnam Speedboat Capsize — What NRIs Need to Know
travel.excerpt: A corporate incentive trip to Phu Quoc Island turned fatal when a packed speedboat overturned in rough seas, exposing dangerous gaps in Southeast Asia's maritime safety enforcement.
travel.image_caption: Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam — the area where a speedboat carrying Indian tourists capsized on July 11 (Wikimedia Commons)
travel.nri_angle: Southeast Asia has become the fastest-growing vacation destination for Indian travelers, with Vietnam alone seeing Indian tourist arrivals surge in recent years. This tragedy is a direct safety warning for the millions of NRIs and India-based travelers booking island-hopping excursions across the region.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: United Airlines Eyes Nonstop Flights From San Francisco to Delhi and Bangalore
travel.excerpt: The rumored ultra-long-haul routes would give Bay Area's half-million Indian Americans their first US carrier option to India's tech capital — and could become among the most profitable flights in aviation.
travel.image_caption: A United Airlines Boeing 787 Dreamliner, the aircraft type expected to operate the rumored India routes
travel.nri_angle: Bay Area is home to over 400,000 Indian Americans — many of them tech professionals who shuttle between Silicon Valley and Bangalore. A United nonstop on SFO-BLR would end decades of inconvenient one-stop itineraries via the Gulf or Europe for this corridor.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Emirates Plans to Deploy Its A380 Superjumbo on Hyderabad Route After 25 Years in the City
travel.excerpt: Telangana's chief minister pitched MRO investments and expanded frequencies as the Dubai carrier proposes its flagship double-decker for one of India's fastest-growing tech corridors.
travel.image_caption: An Emirates Airbus A380 — the world's largest passenger aircraft that could soon fly the Hyderabad-Dubai route
travel.nri_angle: Hyderabad is the fourth-largest source of Indian immigrants to the US, with a massive Telugu-speaking community concentrated in the tech corridors of New Jersey, Texas, and the Bay Area. An A380 on the Hyderabad-Dubai route would dramatically increase seat capacity on a key NRI travel corridor, particularly for connecting flights onward to the US.

travel.title: India-to-US Travel Falls 4% — and Indian Globetrotters Are Finding New Favorites
travel.excerpt: As US arrivals from India record the steepest decline among major source markets, travelers are shifting budgets to the UK, Japan, South Korea, and a string of visa-friendly surprises.

travel.nri_angle: NRIs may notice fewer visiting relatives this summer — and the reasons go beyond airfare, from stricter US border scrutiny to a weakening rupee making America the priciest option on the board.

travel.title: Five-Star Hotels Abroad Cost 23% Less Than in America — Here's How NRIs Can Cash In
travel.excerpt: The 2026 Hotels.com Price Index reveals that luxury travelers who book internationally save an average of $120 a night — and India's monsoon season makes the math even better.

travel.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing a trip home or a summer getaway, the data is clear: a five-star week in India or Southeast Asia costs less than a three-star week in most US cities — and monsoon-season pricing in India sweetens the deal further.

travel.title: Air New Zealand and Air India Are Building a Bridge to Auckland — Direct Flights Targeted by 2028
travel.excerpt: A 16-route codeshare is live, marketing teams are deploying to Indian cities, and both carriers say direct India-New Zealand flights will follow once demand and aircraft deliveries align.

travel.nri_angle: Over 80,000 Indians visited New Zealand last year, a 23% jump from pre-pandemic levels — and for the fast-growing Indian community across Australasia, a nonstop route would transform an 18-hour two-stop journey into a single overnight flight.

travel.title: Air India Cuts Flights to Chicago, San Francisco, and Toronto as Fuel Costs Bite

travel.image_caption: An Air India Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner on the tarmac
travel.nri_angle: The Delhi-Chicago suspension and SFO/Toronto reductions directly hit NRI corridors — Chicago has one of America's largest Indian populations, and SFO serves the Bay Area's massive tech diaspora.

travel.title: Navi Mumbai Airport Gets Its First International Flight on Tuesday
travel.excerpt: Air India Express will fly twice weekly to Abu Dhabi from July 15, making Maharashtra's newest airport an international gateway — and giving Mumbai's eastern suburbs a far shorter ride to the Gulf.
travel.image_caption: Navi Mumbai International Airport terminal building in Maharashtra
travel.nri_angle: For NRIs from Navi Mumbai, Thane, and Pune — especially the large Maharashtrian and Gujarati diaspora in the Gulf — this eliminates the painful trek across Mumbai to Chhatrapati Shivaji airport.

travel.title: Georgia Is Europe's Best-Kept Secret for NRIs — and Your US Visa Gets You In
travel.excerpt: Indian visitor arrivals to Georgia surged 40% last year. Visa-free entry for US, UK, and Schengen visa holders, direct IndiGo flights from Delhi, and costs that undercut Western Europe by half are turning Tbilisi into a diaspora favourite.
travel.image_caption: Panoramic view of Tbilisi, Georgia's capital, with the Kura River and historic Old Town
travel.nri_angle: NRIs holding US, UK, or Schengen visas can enter Georgia visa-free for up to a year — no additional paperwork, no e-visa fees. Combined with IndiGo's nonstop Delhi-Tbilisi flights and costs 50-60% below Western Europe, it's an ideal short-break for diaspora families.
